## Natural history notes

A small ichneumon wasp characterized by its slender body, long antennae, narrow waist, clear wings, and banded legs that give the species its “annulipes” name. In Florida, it is likely found in gardens, fields, forest edges, pine flatwoods, and other vegetated habitats where moth and butterfly larvae are present. It is a parasitoid rather than a nest-building wasp; females lay eggs on or in caterpillar hosts, and the developing larvae feed on the host, helping regulate Lepidoptera populations within the broader insect community.
